It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6303, https://go.dev/issue/80213, https://go.dev/cl/797040. The advisory's vulnerable code is in the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package: NewServerConn, (*connection).serverAuthenticate. Read every published alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 to the current 0.35.0-r2 (there is no 0.33.1-r4), each for x86_64 and aarch64 (72 packages), every download checked against the checksum in the package index. Each package holds two files, /usr/bin/alertmanager and /usr/bin/amtool, statically linked Go programs (no ELF interpreter and no dynamic section) with no ELF symbol table (linked with -ldflags "-s -w"; the Go function table is present), built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The Go build information lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.47.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r3, v0.49.0 in 0.31.1-r4, v0.50.0 in 0.31.1-r5 to 0.32.1-r1, v0.52.0 in 0.32.1-r2 to 0.32.2-r0, v0.53.0 in 0.33.0-r0 to 0.33.1-r1, v0.54.0 in 0.33.1-r2 to 0.33.1-r3, v0.55.0 in 0.33.1-r5 to 0.34.0-r3, v0.56.0 in 0.34.0-r4, v0.57.0 in 0.34.0-r5 to 0.34.1-r1 and v0.58.0 in 0.34.1-r2 to 0.35.0-r2. The function names the Go linker records in each program (its pclntab, read with a debug/gosym reader) were searched in all 72 packages, leaving out the standard library's own copies under vendor/golang.org/x/: the only golang.org/x/crypto packages with functions in them are bcrypt and blowfish in alertmanager and bcrypt in amtool, and no build contains any function from golang.org/x/crypto/ssh or its subpackages (including ssh/agent and ssh/knownhosts), so none of the advisory's vulnerable functions is present, including in the builds whose golang.org/x/crypto version is before v0.55.0. A string search of every binary, which also covers the names of inlined functions, finds golang.org/x/crypto names in each binary but no golang.org/x/crypto/ssh name. Positive control: the same reader finds runtime.main and golang.org/x/crypto/bcrypt functions in every binary of every build, and, in a test program built for linux/amd64 with -ldflags "-s -w" against golang.org/x/crypto v0.50.0 that calls the advisory's functions, finds ssh.NewServerConn and ssh.(*connection).serverAuthenticate. The vulnerable code is not compiled into any published build of this package.

Read the Go build information and the function table of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Each package holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/build. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index, every entry with the same source commit and installed size as 2.19.1-r0; the copy the repository serves was read. The build information of /usr/bin/build lists golang.org/x/crypto, but no build links its SSH server: no function table contains golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.NewServerConn or (*connection).serverAuthenticate, the functions the advisory lists. The same search finds the SSH client function golang.org/x/crypto/ssh.Dial in /usr/bin/build in every build, so /usr/bin/build uses golang.org/x/crypto/ssh only as an SSH client.

CVE-2026-56854 (GO-2026-6303): golang.org/x/crypto/ssh before 0.55.0 enforced the source-address critical option only for the Permissions returned by PublicKeyCallback and VerifiedPublicKeyCallback, so a source-address restriction returned by the password, keyboard-interactive, no-client-auth or GSSAPI callbacks was ignored. It is fixed in golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 by a commit that moves the check to the end of each authentication attempt in the server's authentication loop in ssh/server.go: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6303, https://go.dev/issue/80213, https://go.dev/cl/797040, https://github.com/golang/crypto/commit/e557b08ec2b4f5dd00f38356919fc7b051dd88f8. The Go vulnerability database lists NewServerConn and connection.serverAuthenticate in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh as the affected functions. We read every published external-dns-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64: 33 versions, 0.20.0-r0 to 0.24.0-r5, each matching its repository index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. In every version the four external-dns packages (external-dns, external-dns-dev, external-dns-fips and external-dns-fips-dev) and both architectures embed the same module versions. Its Go build information lists the golang.org/x/crypto module (v0.45.0 to v0.58.0 across these builds), but none of the builds links golang.org/x/crypto/ssh. A Go function-table (pclntab) reader, which finds runtime.main in every build, finds no function of the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package in any build. The only exception is the init function of the separate golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/terminal package in 0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r13, a wrapper around golang.org/x/term that does not contain the affected code. A byte search of every program, which also catches inlined names, finds no symbol name of the golang.org/x/crypto/ssh package itself. As a positive control, we built test programs for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 against golang.org/x/crypto v0.54.0, the last affected release, that call NewServerConn with a PasswordCallback. In them the same reader finds NewServerConn, (*connection).serverAuthenticate and checkSourceAddress, the code the fix changes, and the byte search finds golang.org/x/crypto/ssh symbol names. None of the advisory's affected functions is present in any published build.
